_comment: Pinned descriptor AND provenance for the Oniro distribution HAP set.
This single committed file is the Eclipse Bucket-4a provenance: per app it
pins git + branch + sha (source-repo / source-sha), the global build_cmd, and
the license. build-oniro-haps.sh consumes it to CLONE each app from its pinned
remote into out/oniro-haps/src/<app> and build that, so the release is
reproducible from upstream (not from local working-tree state).
SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH: the colocated BUILD.gn also reads this file
(read_file at gn-gen time) and generates one ohos_prebuilt_etc per module
from 'dest' + 'install_dir' (target name = dest with .hap -> _hap). There is
no per-app gating: oniro_install_custom_haps takes the whole list or none of
it. Renaming these keys is a BUILD.gn interface change.
The built HAP binaries are NOT committed (see haps/.gitignore); only this file
is. A signed HAP is not bit-reproducible (hapsigner nonce) and Eclipse does not
redistribute it, so no per-HAP sha256 is pinned here; the driver writes
haps/SHA256SUMS (gitignored) for local verification.
'output' is the EXACT signed-HAP filename hvigor emits for that module (an
infix may disambiguate the wanted variant from co-built ones). Signing is
deterministic and host-independent: the driver nulls
each app's embedded signingConfig (encrypted passwords tied to per-machine
DevEco material fail off-host), builds the UNSIGNED hap, then signs with the
public OpenHarmony test keys (developtools/hapsigner, password 123456) at the
app's 'apl'; bundle name comes from each module's install_dir. An app with
'self_signed': true opts out of all of that and keeps its own signingConfig,
for apps whose committed signing material works off-host and whose exact
certificate or provision profile must be preserved.
WIRING: BUILD.gn's group('oniro_custom_haps') is listed in the product's
bundle.json sub_component (vendor/oniro/hybris_generic). No
applications/standard/hap patch is needed for the ADD-ON apps. The camera,
settingsdata and settings are the exception: each replaces a stock hap
installing the same path, so a product-scoped patch there drops camera_hap,
settingsData_hap and settings_hap under the same gn arg.
'cert' (optional, tree-relative) is a PEM chain for the public test key to
sign with instead of hapsigner's own certificate. Keep keys of this file
plain identifiers: gn's read_file turns JSON object keys into identifiers,
so a key that is, say, a path fails gn gen.
The set is OPT-IN: BUILD.gn
generates no targets unless oniro_install_custom_haps=true (oniro_haps.gni),
and preinstall-config only adds the matching BMS entries in that case.
LICENSING / RELEASE SCOPE: the default product build installs none of the
apps below, so the release redistributes no Oniro-built HAP and their
licences are not the product's to satisfy. The app store is
GPL-3.0-or-later, which is why shipping it by default was withdrawn: it is
incompatible with the Apache-2.0 posture of the product image. Anyone who
opts in with oniro_install_custom_haps=true becomes the distributor of the
resulting image and takes on the obligations of every licence listed here.

apps.name: appstore
apps.license_evidence: LICENSE at the pinned sha is the GPLv3 text; source headers carry the FSF 'either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version' grant. Upstream copyright: westinyang (https://gitee.com/ohos-dev).

apps.name: florisboard
apps.license_evidence: UNCONFIRMED. The pinned tree carries NO LICENSE file; its README states only that upstream FlorisBoard is Apache-2.0 and that the port 'keeps the same license for the reused data'. A LICENSE file must be added to the source repository before this app can be treated as Apache-2.0 licensed.

apps.name: camera
apps.license_evidence: Fork of applications/standard/camera (eclipse-oniro-mirrors/applications_camera); LICENSE at the pinned sha is Apache-2.0, and the fork adds only the rotation fix, a compileSdkVersion build fix and a product override of the recorder's video source type (const.oniro.camera.video_source) and video orientation from the lens's sensor orientation, and replaces upstream's fixed test location (Wuhan) on photos with the camera's real one, on top of upstream.
apps.build_cmd: hvigorw assembleHap --mode module -p module=phone@default,picker@default -p product=default -p buildMode=release --no-daemon
apps._note: Replaces the STOCK com.ohos.camera instead of adding an app, so applications/standard/hap drops camera_hap and cameraPicker_hap under the same gn arg -- both pairs install app/com.ohos.camera/{Camera,cameraPicker}.hap. The picker is built from the same fork because bms installs a bundle dir as one unit and rejects modules whose apiReleaseType differs: the stock sceneboard picker is 'Beta' (SDK 26.0.0.37), a rebuild against the in-tree SDK is 'Release', and mixing them fails preinstall with 9568258 'releaseType not same'. 'self_signed': true keeps the app's own signingConfig instead of the null-and-resign path: it commits working signing material (signature/OpenHarmony.p12 + camera.p7b) whose profile is an 'os_integration' one carrying a Camera distribution certificate that the generic UnsgnedReleasedProfileTemplate cannot reproduce, and com.ohos.camera has an app_signature entry in install_list_capability.json granting allowAppUsePrivilegeExtension, so the chain must stay byte-identical to the stock hap's (leaf 'OpenHarmony Application Release', SHA256 0716E4E8C9B8CEEF6A974CD2289D5C4C668A5B41FA5DF8C0542DCB72602371F5). The per-app 'build_cmd' targets the two modules that ship (phone, picker) and forces release mode; a debug build carries ets/sourceMaps.map and an unoptimised modules.abc and comes out ~9 MB larger.

apps.name: settingsdata
apps.license_evidence: Fork of applications/standard/settings_data (eclipse-oniro-mirrors/applications_settings_data); LICENSE at the pinned sha is Apache-2.0, and the fork adds only a build-system port, one default setting and a fix to the default seeding on top of upstream.
apps.build_cmd: hvigorw assembleHap --mode module -p module=entry@default -p product=default -p buildMode=release --no-daemon
apps._note: Replaces the STOCK com.ohos.settingsdata instead of adding an app, so applications/standard/hap drops settingsData_hap under the same gn arg -- both install app/com.ohos.settingsdata/SettingsData.hap. The fork ports the project to the current hvigor project model and seeds lockscreen_sounds_enabled=0 in default_settings.json (SceneBoard's lock/unlock sounds, in the per-user table; upstream 7.0's DataExtAbility table-from-URI fix 9fd7922 makes the boot-time non-silent fallback read that table too). It also fixes upstream seeding: the first-startup flag key (isFirstStartup vs isFirstStartUp) and the un-awaited per-key inserts made every provider start re-insert all defaults, an existing key is never seeded again, and a table without a section is skipped. On top of upstream OpenHarmony-7.0-Release ab30e84, which no longer seeds device_provisioned / user_setup_complete because the startup guide sets them; Oniro does not preinstall the startup guide, so the fork seeds both again (left at 0, call_manager rejects every incoming call). 'profile' signs with the app's own committed provision profile instead of one generated from the template: it is an os_integration profile carrying ACLs (MANAGE_SECURE_SETTINGS, INSTALL_BUNDLE, MANAGE_BLUETOOTH) and AllowAppUsePrivilegeExtension that the template cannot reproduce, and its distribution certificate is what install_list_capability.json pins as com.ohos.settingsdata's app_signature (8E93863F...). The signing key is the public OpenHarmony test key, as for the stock hap's profile. 'apl' is unused when 'profile' is set (the profile carries it).

apps.name: settings
apps.license_evidence: Fork of applications/standard/settings (eclipse-oniro-mirrors/applications_settings); LICENSE at the pinned sha is Apache-2.0, and the fork adds only a compileSdkVersion build fix and the About card image on top of upstream. That image shows the Oniro logo, a trademark of the Eclipse Foundation (branding/LOGO-NOTICE.txt), scaled only, as the trademark policy requires.
apps.build_cmd: hvigorw assembleHap --mode module -p module=phone@default -p product=default -p buildMode=debug --no-daemon
apps._note: Replaces the STOCK com.ohos.settings instead of adding an app, so applications/standard/hap drops settings_hap under the same gn arg -- both install app/com.ohos.settings/Settings.hap. The fork's only functional change is feature/aboutdevice video_bg.png, the background of the Settings > About card (ScreenItemComponent), which carried the OpenHarmony logo; branding/make_about_card.py composes the Oniro one. Upstream's source is the one the sceneboard prebuilt was built from (same versionCode 601001600; a rebuild has the same entries and module.json, apart from SDK patch level and apiReleaseType). The prebuilt is a DEBUG build (buildMode debug, ets/sourceMaps.map, no obfuscation), so the per-app build_cmd builds debug too: a release build applies obfuscation-rules.txt, which the prebuilt never ran with. 'profile' signs with upstream's committed provision profile, byte-identical to the one embedded in the stock hap (system_basic, hos_system_app, its ACLs, and the distribution certificate install_list_capability.json pins as app_signature EB5DBE52...). 'cert' (tree-relative) is the stock certificate chain, the 2022 re-issue of the public test key (leaf 0716E4E8...) that the in-tree camera source carries, so the hap carries the stock chain and profile. 'apl' is unused when 'profile' is set.

apps.name: flashlight
apps.license_evidence: LICENSE at the pinned sha is the Apache-2.0 text; the source files written for Oniro carry the Apache-2.0 header.
apps._note: Super Bright Flashlight 1.1.0, the same app the Oniro App Store distributes (bundle com.huawei.ohos.superbrightflashlight, kept so store updates reach the preinstalled copy). It has two lights: the flash LED through the public CameraManager.setTorchMode (no permission needed; on/off only) and the screen at a chosen brightness and colour. The SceneBoard Control Center's flashlight tile is UI-only in the prebuilt 7.0 SceneBoard (its tap never calls setTorchMode), so this app is how the user switches the torch. It replaces org.oniroproject.flashlight (github.com/frankplus/oniro-flashlight), whose history was merged into this repository.
